name: Ben Johnson
milestone_by_age_26: Won two silver medals at the 1982 Commonwealth Games in Brisbane at age 20, marking his first international success in elite sprinting.
starting_point: Born in Falmouth, Jamaica in 1961; emigrated to Canada in 1976 and grew up in the Lawrence Heights community of Toronto, a working-class immigrant neighborhood.
current_position: Former sprinter, stripped of 1988 Olympic gold for doping; retired from competition and later worked as a coach and released an autobiography in 2010.

trajectory.title: Emigrated to Canada
trajectory.description: Moved from Jamaica to Canada at age 14, settling in the Lawrence Heights community of Toronto.

trajectory.title: Joined Scarborough Optimists track club
trajectory.description: Began training under coach Charlie Francis at the Scarborough Optimists track club, entering national competition.

trajectory.title: Two silver medals at Commonwealth Games
trajectory.description: Won silver in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the 1982 Brisbane Commonwealth Games, his first major international success.

trajectory.title: Two bronze medals at Los Angeles Olympics
trajectory.description: Won bronze in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the 1984 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: World Indoor champion at 60m
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 60m at the 1985 World Indoor Championships in Paris.

trajectory.title: Commonwealth Games gold medals
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the 1986 Edinburgh Commonwealth Games, beating Carl Lewis in Moscow with 9.95.

trajectory.title: World Championship gold and world record
trajectory.description: Won the 100m at the 1987 World Championships in Rome with a world record of 9.83 seconds, defeating Carl Lewis.

trajectory.title: Seoul Olympics doping scandal
trajectory.description: Won the 100m Olympic final in 9.79 but was stripped of the gold medal three days later after testing positive for stanozolol.

trajectory.title: Comeback attempt
trajectory.description: Returned to competition after a two-year ban, making the Canadian squad for the 1992 Barcelona Olympics.

trajectory.title: Lifetime ban for doping
trajectory.description: Received a lifetime ban from competition after a second positive doping test, ending his athletic career.

name: Ivan Lendl
milestone_by_age_26: Won junior singles titles at both Roland-Garros and Wimbledon in 1978 at age 18, earning the world No. 1 junior ranking; turned professional the same year and won seven ATP singles titles in 1980 at age 20.
starting_point: Born in 1960 in Ostrava, Czechoslovakia to a tennis family; his father Jiri was a top-ranked Czech player and his mother Olga was also a tennis player.
current_position: Retired professional tennis player; 8-time Grand Slam champion; later became a coach, notably coaching Andy Murray to multiple Grand Slam titles.

trajectory.title: Junior Grand Slam and turned pro
trajectory.description: Won junior titles at Roland-Garros and Wimbledon, earning the world No. 1 junior ranking, and turned professional the same year.

trajectory.title: Seven ATP singles titles
trajectory.description: Won seven ATP singles titles including three consecutive weeks of tournament wins, establishing himself on the pro tour.

trajectory.title: First Grand Slam final
trajectory.description: Reached his first Grand Slam final at the French Open, losing to Björn Borg in five sets; won ten titles that year.

trajectory.title: First Grand Slam title at French Open
trajectory.description: Won his first Grand Slam singles title at the 1984 French Open, defeating John McEnroe in a dramatic five-set comeback.

trajectory.title: US Open champion and world No. 1
trajectory.description: Won the US Open and ascended to the world No. 1 ranking, beginning a period of dominance.

trajectory.title: French Open and US Open champion
trajectory.description: Won the French Open and US Open, cementing his status as the dominant player in men's tennis.

trajectory.title: Australian Open champion
trajectory.description: Won the Australian Open, his 8th and final Grand Slam singles title.

trajectory.title: Second Australian Open title
trajectory.description: Won his second Australian Open, defeating Stefan Edberg in the final.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional tennis
trajectory.description: Retired from professional tennis with 94 career singles titles and 270 weeks at world No. 1.

trajectory.title: Coaching Andy Murray
trajectory.description: Began coaching Andy Murray, helping him win the 2012 US Open and 2013 Wimbledon, his first Grand Slam titles.

name: Rubens Barrichello
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1991 British Formula Three Championship at age 19 as the youngest champion in the category's history, after winning the Formula Opel Lotus Euroseries in 1990 at age 18, and made his Formula One debut with Jordan in 1993 at age 21.
starting_point: Born in São Paulo, Brazil in 1972; received his first kart from his grandfather at age 6 and began competitive karting at age 9.
current_position: Brazilian racing driver competing in the Stock Car Pro Series; two-time Stock Car champion (2014, 2022); F1 commentator and broadcaster.

trajectory.title: Began competitive karting
trajectory.description: Started karting and soon became Brazilian Junior Karting Champion, winning multiple national and São Paulo titles through the 1980s.

trajectory.title: Formula Opel Lotus Euroseries champion
trajectory.description: Moved to Europe and won the Formula Opel Lotus Euroseries with Draco Racing in his first season.

trajectory.title: British Formula Three champion
trajectory.description: Won the British Formula Three Championship with West Surrey Racing, becoming the youngest champion in the category's history.

trajectory.title: International F3000 rookie season
trajectory.description: Competed in International Formula 3000, finishing third in the championship despite a major crash at Enna.

trajectory.title: Formula One debut with Jordan
trajectory.description: Made his F1 debut at the South African Grand Prix with Jordan, becoming one of the youngest F1 drivers at the time.

trajectory.title: First F1 podium and pole position
trajectory.description: Achieved his maiden podium at the Pacific Grand Prix and took pole position at the Belgian Grand Prix; survived a frightening crash at Imola.

trajectory.title: Joined Ferrari and first F1 victory
trajectory.description: Signed with Ferrari to partner Michael Schumacher and won his first Grand Prix at the 2000 German Grand Prix.

trajectory.title: Runner-up in World Championship
trajectory.description: Finished runner-up to Schumacher in the 2002 F1 World Championship, contributing to Ferrari's dominant era.

trajectory.title: Brawn GP title challenge
trajectory.description: Drove for Brawn GP and finished third in the 2009 World Championship, nearly challenging teammate Jenson Button for the title.

trajectory.title: Retired from Formula One
trajectory.description: Left F1 after 19 seasons and 322 Grand Prix starts, the most in F1 history at the time.

trajectory.title: Stock Car Pro Series champion
trajectory.description: Won the Brazilian Stock Car Pro Series championship in his second season in the series.

name: Paolo Rossi
milestone_by_age_26: Became the first player to top the scoring charts in Serie B (21 goals, 1976-77) and Serie A (24 goals, 1977-78) in consecutive seasons at age 21-22, and won the Silver Ball as second-best player at the 1978 FIFA World Cup while becoming the world's most expensive player.
starting_point: Born in 1956 in Prato, Tuscany, Italy; discovered by Juventus scout Italo Allodi at age 15 playing for an amateur side.
current_position: Died on December 9, 2020 at age 64 from complications of lung cancer; final role: football commentator and pundit.

trajectory.title: Juventus youth and first-team debut
trajectory.description: Signed by Juventus as a teenager and made his first-team debut in a Coppa Italia match against Cesena on May 1, 1974.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough at Vicenza
trajectory.description: Loaned to Lanerossi Vicenza, moved from wing to centre-forward by coach Fabbri, and won the Serie B Golden Boot with 21 goals.

trajectory.title: Serie A top scorer and World Cup Silver Ball
trajectory.description: Scored 24 goals to top Serie A scoring, then won the Silver Ball at the 1978 World Cup as Italy reached the semi-finals.

trajectory.title: Totonero match-fixing scandal
trajectory.description: Implicated in the Totonero betting scandal and banned from football for three years, later reduced to two on appeal.

trajectory.title: World Cup hero and Ballon d'Or
trajectory.description: Returned from ban to score 6 goals at the 1982 World Cup, winning the Golden Boot, Golden Ball, and the Ballon d'Or as Italy won the tournament.

trajectory.title: European Cup with Juventus
trajectory.description: Won the European Cup with Juventus, scoring in the final against Liverpool, completing a rare World Cup-Champions League-Ballon d'Or treble.

trajectory.title: Retirement from football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after spells with Juventus and AC Milan.

trajectory.title: Death
trajectory.description: Died on December 9, 2020 from complications of lung cancer, mourned as one of Italy's greatest football heroes.

name: Miki Matsubara
milestone_by_age_26: Released her debut single 'Mayonaka no Door (Stay With Me)' on November 5, 1979 at age 19, which became a commercial hit reaching No. 28 on the Oricon Singles Chart and establishing her as a next-gen city pop artist with Pony Canyon.
starting_point: Born in 1959 in Kishiwada, Osaka, Japan; her mother was a jazz singer with Crazy Cats and her father was a hospital board member; began piano at age 3.
current_position: Died on October 7, 2004 at age 44 from cervical cancer; posthumously became a global city pop icon after 'Mayonaka no Door' went viral on TikTok in 2020.

trajectory.title: Joined first rock band
trajectory.description: Entered Poole Gakuin Junior High School and joined the rock band Kurei, developing her interest in rock music.

trajectory.title: Active keyboardist in high school band
trajectory.description: Became keyboard player of the Yoshinoya Band, performing at the live house Takutaku in Kyoto.

trajectory.title: Moved to Tokyo to pursue music
trajectory.description: Left Osaka for Tokyo to pursue a singing career, performing at venues while studying and working part-time.

trajectory.title: Debut single 'Mayonaka no Door'
trajectory.description: Released debut single 'Mayonaka no Door (Stay With Me)' on November 5, reaching No. 28 on the Oricon chart and launching her career with Pony Canyon.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Pocket Park'
trajectory.description: Released her first studio album 'Pocket Park,' establishing her as a city pop artist with jazz-influenced pop.

trajectory.title: Anime theme song work
trajectory.description: Contributed opening and ending theme songs for the anime Gu-Gu Ganmo under the name Suzie Matsubara.

trajectory.title: Shift to composing for other artists
trajectory.description: Paused her performing career to focus on composing and writing lyrics for other artists and anime soundtracks.

trajectory.title: Retirement from music
trajectory.description: Retired and severed all connections to the music world after being diagnosed with cervical cancer.

trajectory.title: Death from cervical cancer
trajectory.description: Died on October 7, 2004 in Sakai, Osaka, at age 44.

trajectory.title: Posthumous viral fame
trajectory.description: 'Mayonaka no Door' went viral globally on TikTok and YouTube, sparking an international city pop revival and introducing her music to millions of new listeners.

name: Agnetha Fältskog
milestone_by_age_26: Her self-penned debut single 'Jag var sa kar' ('I Was So in Love') topped the Swedish chart on January 28, 1968 at age 17, selling over 80,000 copies and knocking The Beatles from the number one spot, leading to her self-titled debut album later that year.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in Jönköping, Sweden; father Ingvar was an amateur dramatics enthusiast who encouraged her early performing; began piano and composing songs as a child.
current_position: Retired Swedish singer; member of ABBA, one of the best-selling music acts in history; reunited with ABBA for the 2021 album 'Voyage'; resides on Ekerö island near Stockholm.

trajectory.title: Joined Bernt Enghardt band
trajectory.description: Began singing with a local dance band in Jönköping, writing original songs including 'Jag var så kär.'

trajectory.title: Debut single topped Swedish charts
trajectory.description: Her self-penned debut single 'Jag var så kär' topped the Swedish chart on January 28, selling over 80,000 copies and knocking The Beatles from No. 1.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Agnetha Fältskog'
trajectory.description: Released her self-titled debut album, establishing her as one of Sweden's most popular pop artists.

trajectory.title: Married Björn Ulvaeus
trajectory.description: Married Björn Ulvaeus, forming the personal and professional partnership that would become ABBA.

trajectory.title: ABBA formation and early recordings
trajectory.description: Began recording with Björn, Benny Andersson, and Anni-Frid Lyngstad; the group that would become ABBA started taking shape.

trajectory.title: ABBA wins Eurovision
trajectory.description: ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo,' launching their international career and making them global superstars.

trajectory.title: ABBA global domination
trajectory.description: ABBA releases 'Greatest Hits' and 'Arrival,' including hits like 'Dancing Queen' and 'Knowing Me, Knowing You,' cementing their status as one of the world's biggest bands.

trajectory.title: ABBA unofficial breakup
trajectory.description: ABBA effectively disbanded in December 1982; Agnetha pursued a solo career with three albums in the 1980s.

trajectory.title: Solo comeback album 'My Colouring Book'
trajectory.description: Returned to recording after a 16-year hiatus with 'My Colouring Book,' which charted internationally.

trajectory.title: ABBA 'Voyage' reunion album
trajectory.description: Reunited with ABBA to release 'Voyage,' their first studio album in 40 years, accompanied by a revolutionary digital concert residency in London.

name: Stefan Edberg
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Grand Slam singles title at the 1985 Australian Open at age 19, defeating defending champion Mats Wilander in straight sets, after achieving the junior Grand Slam in 1983.
starting_point: Born in 1966 in Västervik, Sweden; began playing tennis at age 7 in 1973, following in the footsteps of his idol Björn Borg.
current_position: Retired professional tennis player; 6-time Grand Slam singles champion; former world No. 1; coached Roger Federer from 2014-2015.

trajectory.title: Junior Grand Slam
trajectory.description: Won all four junior Grand Slam singles titles in 1983, becoming the first and only player to achieve a junior Grand Slam in the Open Era.

trajectory.title: First ATP title and Olympic exhibition gold
trajectory.description: Won his first ATP singles title in Milan and won the tennis exhibition event at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

trajectory.title: First Grand Slam title at Australian Open
trajectory.description: Won the 1985 Australian Open, defeating world No. 1 Ivan Lendl in the semi-final and Mats Wilander in the final in straight sets.

trajectory.title: Second Australian Open title
trajectory.description: Won his second Australian Open, defeating Pat Cash in a five-set final.

trajectory.title: Wimbledon champion
trajectory.description: Won his first Wimbledon title, defeating Boris Becker in four sets; also reached world No. 1 in doubles.

trajectory.title: World No. 1 and second Wimbledon
trajectory.description: Ascended to the world No. 1 singles ranking and won his second Wimbledon title, again defeating Boris Becker in a five-set final.

trajectory.title: US Open champion
trajectory.description: Won the US Open, defeating Jim Courier in straight sets in the final.

trajectory.title: Second US Open title
trajectory.description: Won his second US Open, defeating Pete Sampras in four sets; reached the final of all four Grand Slams that year.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional tennis
trajectory.description: Retired after 14 years on tour with 41 singles titles, 6 Grand Slams, and 54 consecutive Grand Slam appearances.

trajectory.title: Coaching Roger Federer
trajectory.description: Began coaching Roger Federer, helping him reach the 2014 Wimbledon final and win the 2015 Cincinnati Masters.

name: Riccardo Patrese
milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut at the 1977 Monaco Grand Prix at age 23, having won both the Italian and European Formula 3 championships in 1976 and the Karting World Championship in 1974 at age 20.
starting_point: Born in 1954 in Padua, Italy; started kart racing at age 9; also selected for the Italian national ski team as a teenager.
current_position: Retired Italian racing driver; held the record for most F1 Grand Prix starts (256) for 19 years; lives in Italy.

trajectory.title: Karting World Championship
trajectory.description: Won the Karting World Championship at the Estoril circuit, finishing ahead of future F1 driver Eddie Cheever.

trajectory.title: Italian and European F3 champion
trajectory.description: Won both the Italian and European Formula 3 championships, establishing himself as a top junior racing talent.

trajectory.title: Formula One debut at Monaco
trajectory.description: Made his F1 debut with Shadow at the 1977 Monaco Grand Prix, scoring his first point at the Japanese Grand Prix later that year.

trajectory.title: Moved to Arrows team
trajectory.description: Joined the newly formed Arrows team, developing a reputation for aggressive driving; was controversially blamed for Ronnie Peterson's fatal crash at Monza.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory at Monaco
trajectory.description: Won his first Grand Prix at the 1982 Monaco Grand Prix with Brabham, in a dramatic race where multiple leaders dropped out.

trajectory.title: Second F1 victory in South Africa
trajectory.description: Won the 1983 South African Grand Prix at Kyalami, his second career victory.

trajectory.title: Joined Williams
trajectory.description: Signed with Williams, beginning his most successful period in F1 alongside teammate Nigel Mansell.

trajectory.title: First driver to 200 Grand Prix starts
trajectory.description: Became the first F1 driver to reach 200 Grand Prix starts at the 1990 British Grand Prix.

trajectory.title: World Championship runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished runner-up to Nigel Mansell in the 1992 World Championship, his best-ever championship result.

trajectory.title: Retirement from F1
trajectory.description: Retired from Formula One after 256 Grand Prix starts and 6 victories, holding the record for most F1 starts for 19 years.

name: Goran Bregović
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album with Bijelo Dugme in November 1974 at age 24, which broke the Yugoslav record for best-selling rock album and earned a gold record by February 1975.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina; father was Croatian and mother Serbian; began violin at music school but was expelled; played folk music in kafanas as a teenager.
current_position: Internationally renowned composer and musician; performs worldwide with his Weddings and Funerals Orchestra; continues composing film scores and solo projects.

trajectory.title: Started playing in bands
trajectory.description: Joined school band Izohipse on bass guitar, later moving to Beštije and playing folk music in a kafana to support himself.

trajectory.title: Joined Kodeksi band
trajectory.description: Invited by Željko Bebek to play bass in his band Kodeksi, beginning his serious musical career.

trajectory.title: Founded Bijelo Dugme and debut album
trajectory.description: Founded Bijelo Dugme and released their debut album in November 1974, which broke Yugoslav sales records and earned gold by February 1975.

trajectory.title: Bijelo Dugme dominance
trajectory.description: By the early 1980s, Bijelo Dugme had become the most popular rock band in Yugoslavia, selling millions of records and filling stadiums.

trajectory.title: Disbanded Bijelo Dugme
trajectory.description: Disbanded Bijelo Dugme amid rising nationalist fervor, embarking on a solo career and film composition.

trajectory.title: Film score for 'Time of the Gypsies'
trajectory.description: Composed the score for Emir Kusturica's 'Time of the Gypsies,' launching his internationally acclaimed film composition career.

trajectory.title: Score for 'Underground' (Palme d'Or)
trajectory.description: Composed the score for Kusturica's Palme d'Or-winning film 'Underground,' further cementing his international reputation.

trajectory.title: Score for 'La Reine Margot'
trajectory.description: Composed the score for the Academy Award-nominated film 'La Reine Margot,' expanding his reach to Western European cinema.

trajectory.title: International solo career
trajectory.description: Established himself as a globally touring solo artist with his Weddings and Funerals Orchestra, performing at Carnegie Hall, Royal Albert Hall, and l'Olympia.

name: Lilian Thuram
milestone_by_age_26: Made professional debut with Monaco in Ligue 1 on May 24, 1991 at age 19, won the Coupe de France that season, and by age 26 was a 1998 FIFA World Cup winner with France awarded the Bronze Ball as third best player.
starting_point: Born in 1972 in Pointe-à-Pitre, Guadeloupe, France; moved to metropolitan France as a youth and grew up in the Paris suburbs.
current_position: French author, philanthropist, and former footballer; founder of the Lilian Thuram Foundation promoting education against racism; active public intellectual.

trajectory.title: Professional debut with Monaco
trajectory.description: Made his Ligue 1 debut for AS Monaco on May 24, 1991, and won the Coupe de France in his first season.

trajectory.title: France national team debut
trajectory.description: Earned his first cap for the France national team, beginning a record-setting international career.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Parma
trajectory.description: Joined Parma in Serie A, where he developed into one of the world's best defenders over five seasons.

trajectory.title: World Cup winner and Bronze Ball
trajectory.description: Won the 1998 FIFA World Cup with France, scoring both goals in the semi-final against Croatia and winning the Bronze Ball as third-best player of the tournament.

trajectory.title: UEFA Euro 2000 champion
trajectory.description: Won the 2000 European Championship with France, completing a World Cup-Euro double.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Juventus
trajectory.description: Joined Juventus for a record fee for a defender, winning two Serie A titles (later revoked due to Calciopoli).

trajectory.title: World Cup runner-up and move to Barcelona
trajectory.description: Reached the 2006 World Cup final with France (lost to Italy) and transferred to FC Barcelona.

trajectory.title: Retirement from football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football with 142 caps for France, the national record until surpassed by Hugo Lloris in 2022.

trajectory.title: Founded Lilian Thuram Foundation
trajectory.description: Established his foundation focused on education against racism and discrimination, becoming a prominent public intellectual.

name: Jean Alesi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the French Formula Three Championship in 1987 at age 23, won the International Formula 3000 Championship in 1989 at age 25, debuted in Formula One at the 1989 French Grand Prix finishing fourth, and scored maiden F1 podiums at the opening round and Monaco in 1990 at age 25-26.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Avignon, France to Sicilian immigrant parents; started karting at age 16 and initially aspired to rally driving.
current_position: Retired French racing driver; competed in F1 from 1989-2001 with 1 win and 32 podiums; later competed in DTM and Indianapolis 500.

trajectory.title: Started single-seater racing
trajectory.description: Began racing in the national Renault Five series, initially without major sponsor backing unlike many peers.

trajectory.title: French Formula Three champion
trajectory.description: Won the French F3 Championship with ORECA, driving a Dallara chassis after the team switched from an uncompetitive Martini-Alfa Romeo.

trajectory.title: F3000 champion and F1 debut
trajectory.description: Won the International F3000 Championship with Eddie Jordan's team and made his F1 debut with Tyrrell at the French Grand Prix, finishing fourth.

trajectory.title: Maiden F1 podiums and Senna duel
trajectory.description: Scored podiums at the US Grand Prix in Phoenix (dueling with Ayrton Senna) and at Monaco, establishing himself as a rising F1 star.

trajectory.title: Signed for Ferrari
trajectory.description: Joined Ferrari to partner Alain Prost, fulfilling a childhood dream but joining during a lean period for the Scuderia.

trajectory.title: First and only F1 victory
trajectory.description: Won his sole Grand Prix at the 1995 Canadian Grand Prix with Ferrari, on his 31st birthday.

trajectory.title: Moved to Benetton
trajectory.description: Swapped seats with Michael Schumacher, joining Benetton where he scored 13 podiums across two seasons.

trajectory.title: Retirement from Formula One
trajectory.description: Retired from F1 after spells with Sauber, Prost, and Jordan, ending a 201-race career with 1 win and 32 podiums.

trajectory.title: DTM career
trajectory.description: Joined the German Touring Car Championship (DTM) with Mercedes, competing for five seasons with moderate success.

name: John Deacon
milestone_by_age_26: Released Queen's self-titled debut album in 1973 at age 22 and wrote the international hit 'You're My Best Friend' for A Night at the Opera in 1975 at age 24.
starting_point: Born in 1951 in Leicester, England; father Arthur worked at Norwich Union insurance and encouraged John's interest in electronics; formed first band The Opposition at age 14.
current_position: Retired English musician; bassist of Queen; retired from the music industry in 1997 after Freddie Mercury's death; remains involved in Queen's financial affairs but does not perform.

trajectory.title: Formed first band The Opposition
trajectory.description: Formed a school band called The Opposition, initially on guitar before switching to bass in 1966.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Chelsea College
trajectory.description: Moved to London to study electronics at Chelsea College, University of London, achieving a first-class honours degree.

trajectory.title: Joined Queen
trajectory.description: Auditioned for and joined Queen in January 1971, completing the classic lineup with Freddie Mercury, Brian May, and Roger Taylor.

trajectory.title: Queen's debut album released
trajectory.description: Queen's self-titled debut album was released in 1973, with Deacon credited as 'Deacon John' on bass.

trajectory.title: Wrote 'You're My Best Friend'
trajectory.description: Composed the international hit 'You're My Best Friend' for the album 'A Night at the Opera,' his first major songwriting contribution.

trajectory.title: 'Another One Bites the Dust' global hit
trajectory.description: Wrote 'Another One Bites the Dust,' which became Queen's biggest-selling single and a global crossover hit.

trajectory.title: Wrote 'I Want to Break Free'
trajectory.description: Wrote 'I Want to Break Free,' another Queen classic that became an international hit.

trajectory.title: Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert
trajectory.description: Performed at the Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert in 1992, one of his last public performances with Queen.

trajectory.title: Retired from music industry
trajectory.description: Retired from the music industry after recording 'No-One but You (Only the Good Die Young),' Queen's final recording with Deacon.

name: Oleg Blokhin
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Ballon d'Or as European Footballer of the Year in December 1975 at age 23, having already become the Soviet Top League's standout striker for Dynamo Kyiv and led the team to the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union; joined Dynamo Kyiv's youth academy in 1962 at age 10.
current_position: Ukrainian former football player and manager; managed the Ukraine national team at the 2006 World Cup and Euro 2012; regarded as one of the greatest Soviet/Ukrainian footballers ever.

trajectory.title: Dynamo Kyiv senior debut
trajectory.description: Made his senior debut for Dynamo Kyiv, beginning an 18-year spell at the club that would define his career.

trajectory.title: Olympic bronze and top scorer
trajectory.description: Competed at the 1972 Munich Olympics, winning bronze with the Soviet Union, and became Soviet Top League top scorer.

trajectory.title: Ballon d'Or winner
trajectory.description: Won the Ballon d'Or as European Footballer of the Year, the first Ukrainian and second Soviet player to achieve this, after leading Dynamo Kyiv to the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup.

trajectory.title: UEFA Cup Winners' Cup champion
trajectory.description: Led Dynamo Kyiv to the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup title, scoring in the final against Ferencváros.

trajectory.title: World Cup appearance
trajectory.description: Represented the Soviet Union at the 1982 FIFA World Cup in Spain, scoring 2 goals.

trajectory.title: Second Cup Winners' Cup and World Cup
trajectory.description: Won his second UEFA Cup Winners' Cup with Dynamo Kyiv and played at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico.

trajectory.title: Left Dynamo Kyiv
trajectory.description: After 18 seasons and 266 goals for Dynamo Kyiv, moved to Austrian club Vorwärts Steyr, then Aris Limassol in Cyprus.

trajectory.title: Began managerial career
trajectory.description: Retired as a player and began managing Olympiacos in Greece, later managing PAOK, Ionikos, and the Ukraine national team.

trajectory.title: Managed Ukraine at World Cup
trajectory.description: Led the Ukraine national team to their first-ever FIFA World Cup appearance, reaching the quarter-finals in Germany.

name: Cameron Diaz
milestone_by_age_26: Made her film debut at 21 as the female lead in The Mask (1994), which became one of the top 10 highest-grossing films of the year and launched her as a Hollywood star.
starting_point: Born in 1972 in San Diego, California; father was a Cuban-American oil company foreman, mother an import broker of Italian-German descent; raised in Long Beach and signed with Elite Model Management at 16.
current_position: American actress; returned to acting in 2025 with 'Back in Action' after a decade-long hiatus; films have grossed over $3 billion domestically; married to musician Benji Madden.

trajectory.title: Signed with Elite Model Management
trajectory.description: Began a successful modeling career while in high school, appearing in campaigns for Calvin Klein, Coca-Cola, and Levi's, and living in Paris and Japan.

trajectory.title: Film debut in 'The Mask'
trajectory.description: Made her acting debut with no prior experience as the female lead opposite Jim Carrey in 'The Mask,' which grossed over $350 million worldwide.

trajectory.title: 'My Best Friend's Wedding' success
trajectory.description: Held her own against Julia Roberts in the hit romantic comedy 'My Best Friend's Wedding,' re-establishing her in mainstream Hollywood.

trajectory.title: 'There's Something About Mary' stardom
trajectory.description: Starred in the Farrelly brothers comedy that became a massive box office hit and earned her first Golden Globe nomination, cementing her A-list status.

trajectory.title: Critical acclaim with 'Being John Malkovich'
trajectory.description: Earned critical recognition and a second Golden Globe nomination for Spike Jonze's surrealist film 'Being John Malkovich.'

trajectory.title: Charlie's Angels and Shrek franchise
trajectory.description: Starred in the blockbuster 'Charlie's Angels' and began voicing Princess Fiona in the 'Shrek' franchise, which would span four films.

trajectory.title: Gangs of New York and Vanilla Sky
trajectory.description: Earned Golden Globe nominations for 'Vanilla Sky' (2001) and Martin Scorsese's 'Gangs of New York' (2002), proving dramatic range.

trajectory.title: Acting hiatus
trajectory.description: After starring in 'The Other Woman,' 'Sex Tape,' and 'Annie' in 2014, stepped away from acting to focus on family and wellness.

trajectory.title: Return to acting with 'Back in Action'
trajectory.description: Came out of retirement to star in the Netflix action-comedy 'Back in Action' alongside Jamie Foxx.

name: Eric Cantona
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1988 U21 European Championship with France at age 22, scoring a hat-trick in the quarter-final against England, and transferred to Marseille for a French record fee shortly after.
starting_point: Born in 1966 in Marseille, France; discovered by AJ Auxerre at age 15 while playing for a youth team outside Marseille.
current_position: French actor and former footballer; pursued an acting career after retirement; remains a cultural icon and Manchester United legend.

trajectory.title: Auxerre first-team debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut for AJ Auxerre during the 1983-84 season, having been discovered at age 15.

trajectory.title: U21 European Championship winner
trajectory.description: Won the U21 European Championship with France, scoring a hat-trick in the quarter-final against England; transferred to Marseille for a French record fee.

trajectory.title: Disciplinary issues and bans
trajectory.description: Banned from the national team for a year for criticizing the coach and suspended by Marseille after throwing his shirt at a referee.

trajectory.title: Leeds United and first Premier League title
trajectory.description: Signed for Leeds United, helping them win the last ever Division One Championship in 1991-92.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Manchester United
trajectory.description: Signed for Manchester United for £1.2 million in November 1992, becoming the catalyst for Alex Ferguson's dynasty.

trajectory.title: First Premier League and FA Cup Double
trajectory.description: Won the Premier League and FA Cup double with Manchester United; voted PFA Player of the Year, the first foreign player to win the award.

trajectory.title: Kung-fu kick incident and ban
trajectory.description: Launched a kung-fu kick at a Crystal Palace fan after being sent off, receiving an eight-month ban from football and community service.

trajectory.title: Comeback and second Double
trajectory.description: Returned from ban to lead Manchester United to another Premier League and FA Cup double, scoring the winning goal in the FA Cup final.

trajectory.title: Retirement from football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football at age 30, having won four Premier League titles in five years with Manchester United.

trajectory.title: Acting career begins
trajectory.description: Began a film acting career, appearing in numerous French and international films including 'Elizabeth' (1998) and 'Looking for Eric' (2009).

name: Xabi Alonso
milestone_by_age_26: Captained Real Sociedad to a 2nd-place finish in La Liga in the 2002-03 season at age 21, winning the Best Spanish Player award, and made his debut for the Spain national team in April 2003.
starting_point: Born in 1981 in Tolosa, Basque Country, Spain; son of Periko Alonso, a former Barcelona and Real Sociedad player; grew up in a footballing family.
current_position: Spanish football manager; manager of Chelsea FC; previously managed Bayer Leverkusen to an unbeaten Bundesliga title in 2024; widely regarded as one of the best young managers in the world.

trajectory.title: Real Sociedad debut
trajectory.description: Made his debut for Real Sociedad's first team, having come through their youth system and after a loan spell at Eibar.

trajectory.title: La Liga runners-up and Spain debut
trajectory.description: Captained Real Sociedad to a 2nd-place finish in La Liga, won Best Spanish Player award, and made his Spain national team debut in April 2003.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Liverpool
trajectory.description: Joined Liverpool for £10.5 million under manager Rafa Benítez, immediately becoming a key midfielder.

trajectory.title: Champions League winner
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Champions League with Liverpool in Istanbul, scoring the equalizing goal in the famous 3-3 final against AC Milan.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Joined Real Madrid for £30 million, winning La Liga, two Copa del Rey titles, and another Champions League over five seasons.

trajectory.title: Joined Bayern Munich
trajectory.description: Transferred to Bayern Munich, winning three consecutive Bundesliga titles before retiring in 2017.

trajectory.title: Retirement from playing
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after a decorated playing career with 114 caps for Spain, winning the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012.

trajectory.title: Bayer Leverkusen manager
trajectory.description: Appointed manager of Bayer Leverkusen, transforming the club into a dominant force in German football.

trajectory.title: Invincible Bundesliga title
trajectory.description: Led Bayer Leverkusen to an unprecedented unbeaten Bundesliga season, the first in German football history, winning the domestic double.

trajectory.title: Appointed Chelsea manager
trajectory.description: Accepted the Chelsea managerial position, returning to the Premier League as one of the most sought-after young managers in world football.

name: Ralf Schumacher
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Formula Nippon championship in 1996 at age 21 as the first rookie ever to clinch the title, and entered Formula One with Jordan in 1997 at age 22.
starting_point: Born in 1975 in Hürth, West Germany; younger brother of seven-time F1 champion Michael Schumacher; began karting at age 3 on his parents' go-kart track in Kerpen.
current_position: German former racing driver and broadcaster; F1 commentator for Sky Sport Germany; mentors young drivers in DTM.

trajectory.title: German Junior Kart Championship
trajectory.description: Won the German Junior Kart Championship, following in the footsteps of his older brother Michael.

trajectory.title: German Formula Three
trajectory.description: Finished third in the German Formula Three Championship, progressing through junior single-seater categories.

trajectory.title: Formula Nippon champion as rookie
trajectory.description: Won the Japanese Formula Nippon championship, becoming the first rookie ever to clinch the title.

trajectory.title: F1 debut with Jordan
trajectory.description: Made his Formula One debut with Jordan at the Australian Grand Prix, achieving a podium in only his third race in Argentina.

trajectory.title: Jordan's maiden victory at Spa
trajectory.description: Helped Jordan achieve their first-ever Grand Prix victory with a 1-2 finish at the rain-soaked Belgian Grand Prix with teammate Damon Hill.

trajectory.title: Moved to Williams
trajectory.description: Signed with Williams ahead of their BMW engine partnership, finishing sixth in the championship.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory at San Marino
trajectory.description: Won his first Grand Prix at Imola, the first of three victories that season, finishing fourth in the championship.

trajectory.title: Final F1 victories
trajectory.description: Won two Grands Prix including the French GP from pole position, his final career victories.

trajectory.title: Moved to Toyota
trajectory.description: Joined Toyota Racing, but struggled to match his earlier form over three seasons with the team.

trajectory.title: Left Formula One
trajectory.description: Departed F1 after 11 seasons and 6 Grand Prix victories, joining DTM with Mercedes for five seasons before retiring from motorsport in 2012.

name: Tom Cruise
milestone_by_age_26: Breakthrough leading role in 'Risky Business' (1983) at age 21, which grossed $65 million and earned him a Golden Globe nomination; cemented superstar status with 'Top Gun' (1986) at age 24.
starting_point: Born in 1962 in Syracuse, New York; father was an electrical engineer, mother a teacher; parents divorced when he was 11; moved frequently as a child and struggled with dyslexia.
current_position: American actor and producer; one of Hollywood's most bankable stars with films grossing over $13.3 billion worldwide; known for performing his own dangerous stunts in the Mission: Impossible franchise.

trajectory.title: Film debut in 'Endless Love'
trajectory.description: Made his film debut with a minor role in 'Endless Love' and had a supporting role in 'Taps' the same year.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with 'Risky Business'
trajectory.description: Starred in 'Risky Business,' which grossed $65 million and earned him his first Golden Globe nomination, launching his career as a leading man.

trajectory.title: 'Top Gun' superstar status
trajectory.description: Starred in 'Top Gun,' the highest-grossing film of 1986, cementing his status as a global superstar and sex symbol.

trajectory.title: First Oscar nomination for 'Born on the Fourth of July'
trajectory.description: Received his first Academy Award nomination and won a Golden Globe for his portrayal of Vietnam veteran Ron Kovic in Oliver Stone's film.

trajectory.title: Mission: Impossible franchise launch
trajectory.description: Starred as Ethan Hunt in 'Mission: Impossible,' the first film from his production company Cruise/Wagner Productions, launching a decades-long franchise.

trajectory.title: 'Jerry Maguire' and second Oscar nomination
trajectory.description: Earned his second Academy Award nomination and won a Golden Globe for 'Jerry Maguire,' demonstrating dramatic range.

trajectory.title: 'Magnolia' and third Oscar nomination
trajectory.description: Received his third Academy Award nomination (Best Supporting Actor) for Paul Thomas Anderson's 'Magnolia.'

trajectory.title: 'Top Gun: Maverick' blockbuster
trajectory.description: Starred in 'Top Gun: Maverick,' which grossed over $1.4 billion worldwide and earned critical acclaim, revitalizing his career at age 60.

name: Gabriel Batistuta
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Copa América 1991 with Argentina at age 22, finishing as tournament top scorer with 6 goals, and earned a transfer to Fiorentina in Serie A the same summer.
starting_point: Born in 1969 in Avellaneda, Santa Fe, Argentina; father Omar was a slaughterhouse worker and mother Gloria a school secretary; grew up in Reconquista.
current_position: Argentine former footballer; regarded as one of the greatest strikers of all time; named in FIFA 100; lives in Argentina after retirement.

trajectory.title: Professional debut with Newell's Old Boys
trajectory.description: Made his professional debut with Newell's Old Boys in Argentina, beginning his senior career.

trajectory.title: Moved to Boca Juniors via River Plate
trajectory.description: Transferred from River Plate to Boca Juniors, becoming the league's top scorer in 1990-91 with 23 goals in 29 matches.

trajectory.title: Copa América winner and Fiorentina transfer
trajectory.description: Won Copa América with Argentina as top scorer (6 goals) and transferred to Fiorentina in Serie A the same summer.

trajectory.title: Loyalty to Fiorentina through relegation
trajectory.description: Stayed with Fiorentina after they were relegated to Serie B, helping them return to Serie A the following season.

trajectory.title: Serie A top scorer with 26 goals
trajectory.description: Scored 26 goals in the 1994-95 Serie A season, finishing as the league's top scorer (Capocannoniere).

trajectory.title: Coppa Italia and bronze statue
trajectory.description: Won the Coppa Italia and Supercoppa Italiana with Fiorentina; fans erected a life-size bronze statue in his honor in Florence.

trajectory.title: World Cup and Argentina's all-time top scorer
trajectory.description: Scored 5 goals at the 1998 World Cup, becoming Argentina's all-time leading World Cup scorer with 10 goals across three tournaments.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Roma for record fee
trajectory.description: Joined AS Roma for €36 million, the highest fee ever paid for a player over 30 at the time.

trajectory.title: First Serie A title with Roma
trajectory.description: Won his first and only Serie A championship with AS Roma, scoring 20 goals in his debut season.

trajectory.title: Retirement from football
trajectory.description: Retired after a brief spell with Al-Arabi in Qatar, ending a career with 56 goals in 78 appearances for Argentina.

name: Teofilo Stevenson
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in heavyweight boxing at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 20, followed by World Championship gold in 1974 and a second Olympic gold at the 1976 Montreal Olympics at age 24.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Puerto Padre, Cuba; began boxing as a teenager under the Cuban amateur boxing system; father was a fisherman.
current_position: Died on June 11, 2012 at age 60 from a heart attack; final status: Cuban boxing legend and three-time Olympic gold medalist who never turned professional.

trajectory.title: National boxing champion
trajectory.description: Won the Cuban national heavyweight championship, establishing himself as Cuba's top amateur boxer.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold at Munich
trajectory.description: Won the heavyweight boxing gold medal at the 1972 Munich Olympics, defeating Ion Alexe of Romania in the final.

trajectory.title: World Amateur Championship gold
trajectory.description: Won gold at the first World Amateur Boxing Championships in Havana, cementing his status as the world's best amateur heavyweight.

trajectory.title: Second Olympic gold at Montreal
trajectory.description: Won his second Olympic gold medal at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, defeating Mircea Şimon of Romania in the final.

trajectory.title: Third Olympic gold at Moscow
trajectory.description: Won his third Olympic gold medal at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, becoming one of only three boxers to win three Olympic golds.

trajectory.title: Retirement from boxing
trajectory.description: Retired from competitive boxing, having never turned professional despite lucrative offers, remaining loyal to the Cuban revolution.

trajectory.title: Death
trajectory.description: Died on June 11, 2012 in Havana from a heart attack at age 60, mourned as one of Cuba's greatest sporting heroes.

name: Rowan Atkinson
milestone_by_age_26: First won national attention at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in August 1976 at age 21 with the Oxford Revue, leading to a BBC Radio 3 series and the landmark BBC2 sketch show Not the Nine O'Clock News in October 1979 at age 24, for which he won a BAFTA in 1981.
starting_point: Born in 1955 in Consett/ Gosforth, England; youngest of four boys; father Eric was a farmer and company director; educated at Durham Chorister School and St Bees School before studying electrical engineering at Newcastle and Oxford.
current_position: English actor, comedian, and writer; CBE; best known for Mr. Bean and Blackadder; continues acting in film and television including 'Man vs. Bee' (2022) and 'Wonka' (2023).

trajectory.title: Edinburgh Festival Fringe breakthrough
trajectory.description: Gained national attention at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe performing with the Oxford Revue, leading to television and radio opportunities.

trajectory.title: Not the Nine O'Clock News premiered
trajectory.description: Starred in the landmark BBC2 satirical sketch show 'Not the Nine O'Clock News,' which became a major hit and launched his television career.

trajectory.title: BAFTA win and West End one-man show
trajectory.description: Won a BAFTA for 'Not the Nine O'Clock News' and became the youngest performer to headline a one-man show in London's West End.

trajectory.title: Blackadder series begins
trajectory.description: Began starring in the BBC historical sitcom 'Blackadder' (1983-1989), which became one of the greatest British comedy series of all time.

trajectory.title: Mr. Bean television series
trajectory.description: Launched 'Mr. Bean' on ITV, creating an iconic physical comedy character that became an international phenomenon.

trajectory.title: The Lion King and Four Weddings
trajectory.description: Voiced Zazu in Disney's 'The Lion King' and appeared in 'Four Weddings and a Funeral,' expanding his international film profile.

trajectory.title: Bean: The Movie
trajectory.description: Starred in the 'Bean' feature film, which grossed over $250 million worldwide, bringing Mr. Bean to global cinema audiences.

trajectory.title: Johnny English franchise
trajectory.description: Launched the 'Johnny English' spy comedy film franchise, which would span three films through 2018.

trajectory.title: Olympics opening ceremony
trajectory.description: Performed as Mr. Bean in the London 2012 Olympic Games opening ceremony, seen by billions worldwide.

trajectory.title: Wonka and continued work
trajectory.description: Appeared in the blockbuster film 'Wonka' (2023) and starred in Netflix's 'Man vs. Bee' (2022), continuing his prolific career.

name: Mark Webber
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Formula One debut at the 2002 Australian Grand Prix on March 3, 2002 at age 25, finishing fifth and scoring points — becoming the 51st driver in F1 history to score on debut and the first Australian F1 driver since 1994.
starting_point: Born in 1976 in Queanbeyan, New South Wales, Australia; left Australia at 19 with no sponsors to pursue racing in England; won the Formula Ford Festival at Brands Hatch.
current_position: Australian former racing driver; FIA World Endurance Champion (2015) with Porsche; F1 pundit for Channel 4 and Network 10; driver manager; Officer of the Order of Australia.

trajectory.title: Formula Ford Festival winner
trajectory.description: Won the prestigious Formula Ford Festival at Brands Hatch after moving from Australia to the UK to pursue racing.

trajectory.title: FIA GT Championship runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished runner-up in the FIA GT Championship with AMG Mercedes, winning five of ten races alongside Bernd Schneider.

trajectory.title: F3000 runner-up and F1 test driver
trajectory.description: Finished second in International F3000 with Super Nova Racing and served as test driver for Benetton.

trajectory.title: F1 debut with Minardi
trajectory.description: Made his F1 debut at the Australian Grand Prix, finishing fifth on debut with Minardi, scoring the team's first points in three years.

trajectory.title: First F1 podium at Monaco
trajectory.description: Achieved his first F1 podium finish with Williams at the Monaco Grand Prix, finishing third.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory in Germany
trajectory.description: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the 2009 German Grand Prix with Red Bull Racing, describing it as the proudest moment of his career.

trajectory.title: Third in World Championship
trajectory.description: Finished third in the 2010 F1 World Championship, his best championship result, also winning the Monaco and British Grands Prix.

trajectory.title: Left Formula One
trajectory.description: Retired from F1 after 12 seasons, 9 Grand Prix victories, and 13 pole positions, moving to endurance racing with Porsche.

trajectory.title: WEC World Champion with Porsche
trajectory.description: Won the FIA World Endurance Championship with Porsche, sharing the 919 Hybrid with Timo Bernhard and Brendon Hartley.

trajectory.title: Retirement from motorsport
trajectory.description: Retired from competitive motorsport, becoming a television pundit and driver manager.

name: Gianluigi Buffon
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for Parma on November 19, 1995 at age 17, keeping a clean sheet against reigning champions AC Milan, and by 26 had become a World Cup-winning goalkeeper, Serie A champion, and the world's most expensive goalkeeper transfer.
starting_point: Born in 1978 in Carrara, Italy; came from a family of athletes — his mother was a discus thrower and his father a weightlifter; joined Parma's youth academy.
current_position: Italian former footballer; retired in 2023 at age 45; widely regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers of all time; 2006 World Cup winner; holds record for most Serie A appearances.

trajectory.title: Serie A debut for Parma
trajectory.description: Made his Serie A debut on November 19, 1995, keeping a clean sheet against reigning champions AC Milan.

trajectory.title: UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia with Parma
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Cup, Coppa Italia, and Supercoppa Italiana with Parma, establishing himself as one of the world's best goalkeepers.

trajectory.title: World record transfer to Juventus
trajectory.description: Transferred to Juventus for €52.9 million, the world record fee for a goalkeeper, which stood for 17 years.

trajectory.title: Champions League final and UEFA Club Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Reached the Champions League final with Juventus (lost to AC Milan) and was named UEFA Club Footballer of the Year.

trajectory.title: World Cup winner
trajectory.description: Won the 2006 FIFA World Cup with Italy, conceding only two goals in seven matches (one own-goal, one penalty), and was named to the All-Star Team.

trajectory.title: Stayed with Juventus through relegation
trajectory.description: Remained loyal to Juventus after they were relegated to Serie B due to the Calciopoli scandal, helping them return to Serie A immediately.

trajectory.title: The Best FIFA Goalkeeper award
trajectory.description: Won the inaugural The Best FIFA Men's Goalkeeper award and was named Serie A Footballer of the Year after reaching another Champions League final.

trajectory.title: Moved to Paris Saint-Germain
trajectory.description: Signed with PSG at age 40, winning Ligue 1 and the Trophée des Champions in his only season in France.

trajectory.title: Return to Parma
trajectory.description: Returned to his boyhood club Parma, who had been relegated to Serie B, for a sentimental final spell.

trajectory.title: Retirement from football
trajectory.description: Retired at age 45 after a 28-year professional career with over 1,100 appearances and 176 caps for Italy.

name: Peter Jackson
milestone_by_age_26: Received funding from the New Zealand Film Commission in 1986 (age 24-25) to complete his first feature film Bad Taste, which premiered at the 1988 Cannes Film Festival when he was 26, launching his professional filmmaking career.
starting_point: Born in 1961 in Pukerua Bay, New Zealand; given a Super 8mm camera as a child; no formal film training; worked as a photo-engraver at a Wellington newspaper while making films on weekends.
current_position: New Zealand filmmaker; Sir Peter Jackson ONZ KNZM; fourth-highest-grossing film director of all time with over $6.5 billion worldwide; co-founder of Weta Digital.

trajectory.title: Began making Bad Taste
trajectory.description: Started shooting his first feature film 'Bad Taste' on weekends with friends while working as a newspaper photo-engraver.

trajectory.title: Bad Taste completed and Cannes premiere
trajectory.description: Completed 'Bad Taste' after four years of DIY filmmaking; the film premiered at the 1988 Cannes Film Festival to cult acclaim, launching his career.

trajectory.title: Braindead released
trajectory.description: Released the zombie comedy 'Braindead,' which gained a cult following for its outrageous splatstick humor.

trajectory.title: Heavenly Creatures and Oscar nomination
trajectory.description: Directed 'Heavenly Creatures,' which earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Screenplay and brought him to mainstream prominence.

trajectory.title: The Fellowship of the Ring released
trajectory.description: Released 'The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring,' the first of his landmark trilogy, which became a global phenomenon.

trajectory.title: Three Academy Awards for Return of the King
trajectory.description: Won Academy Awards for Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Adapted Screenplay for 'The Return of the King,' which won 11 Oscars total.

trajectory.title: King Kong remake
trajectory.description: Directed the $207 million remake of 'King Kong,' which grossed over $550 million worldwide.

trajectory.title: The Hobbit trilogy begins
trajectory.description: Began releasing 'The Hobbit' trilogy (2012-2014), which grossed nearly $3 billion worldwide.

trajectory.title: They Shall Not Grow Old
trajectory.description: Directed the acclaimed WWI documentary 'They Shall Not Grow Old,' using restored and colorized archival footage, winning a BAFTA.

trajectory.title: The Beatles: Get Back documentary
trajectory.description: Directed the Emmy-winning documentary series 'The Beatles: Get Back' for Disney+, showcasing his archival restoration techniques.

name: Gheorghe Hagi
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Divizia A (Romanian top division) debut at age 17 in 1982-83 for FC Constanța, then scored 58 goals in 108 appearances for Sportul Studențesc between 1983 and 1986 (ages 18-21), becoming one of Romania's most prodigious young talents and drawing the attention of dictator Ceaușescu before transferring to Steaua București in 1986.
starting_point: Born in 1965 in Săcele, Romania; grew up in the Romanian football system; his talent drew the attention of dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu, who orchestrated his transfer to Steaua București.
current_position: Romanian football manager and former player; head coach of the Romania national team; founded Viitorul Constanța academy and club; nicknamed 'The Maradona of the Carpathians.'

trajectory.title: Divizia A debut for FC Constanța
trajectory.description: Made his Romanian top division debut for FC Constanța at age 17, beginning his professional career.

trajectory.title: Moved to Sportul Studențesc
trajectory.description: Transferred to Sportul Studențesc, where he scored 58 goals in 108 appearances over four seasons, becoming one of Romania's brightest young talents.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Steaua București
trajectory.description: Moved to Romanian powerhouse Steaua București in a transfer orchestrated by dictator Ceaușescu, where he won three league titles and reached the 1989 European Cup final.

trajectory.title: Signed for Real Madrid
trajectory.description: After the Romanian Revolution freed him to leave, signed for Real Madrid following the 1990 World Cup.

trajectory.title: World Cup All-Star Team
trajectory.description: Named to the 1994 FIFA World Cup All-Star Team after leading Romania to the quarter-finals, cementing his global reputation.

trajectory.title: Joined Galatasaray
trajectory.description: Signed for Galatasaray in Turkey, where he would spend five seasons and become a club legend known as 'Comandante.'

trajectory.title: UEFA Cup winner with Galatasaray
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Cup with Galatasaray, defeating Arsenal in the final, and added the UEFA Super Cup by beating Real Madrid.

trajectory.title: Retirement from playing
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after 124 caps and 35 goals for Romania, having played for both Real Madrid and Barcelona.

trajectory.title: Founded Viitorul Constanța
trajectory.description: Founded Romanian club Viitorul Constanța and its namesake football academy, one of the largest in Southeastern Europe.

trajectory.title: Romania national team manager
trajectory.description: Appointed head coach of the Romania national team, returning to manage the country he represented as a player for nearly two decades.

name: Ben Affleck
milestone_by_age_26: Co-wrote and starred in Good Will Hunting (1997) with Matt Damon, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay in March 1998 at age 25, which launched him to mainstream fame.
starting_point: Born in 1972 in Berkeley, California; parents separated when he was 11; moved to Cambridge, Massachusetts; met Matt Damon at age 8; mother was a schoolteacher and father an aspiring playwright.
current_position: American actor and filmmaker; two-time Academy Award winner; known for directing 'Argo' (Best Picture winner) and playing Batman in the DCEU; continues acting and directing.

trajectory.title: Child acting in The Voyage of the Mimi
trajectory.description: Starred in the PBS educational series 'The Voyage of the Mimi' (1984-1988), his first significant acting role.

trajectory.title: Dazed and Confused
trajectory.description: Appeared in Richard Linklater's cult coming-of-age film 'Dazed and Confused,' gaining early attention.

trajectory.title: Good Will Hunting and Academy Award
trajectory.description: Co-wrote and starred in 'Good Will Hunting' with Matt Damon, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay in March 1998, launching him to mainstream fame.

trajectory.title: Armageddon blockbuster
trajectory.description: Starred in Michael Bay's 'Armageddon,' which grossed over $550 million worldwide, establishing him as a leading man.

trajectory.title: Pearl Harbor
trajectory.description: Starred in the big-budget war film 'Pearl Harbor,' which was a box office hit despite mixed reviews.

trajectory.title: Hollywoodland and career comeback
trajectory.description: Made a career comeback with 'Hollywoodland,' winning the Volpi Cup for Best Actor at Venice and earning a Golden Globe nomination.

trajectory.title: Directorial debut with Gone Baby Gone
trajectory.description: Made his critically acclaimed directorial debut with 'Gone Baby Gone,' adapted from the Dennis Lehane novel.

trajectory.title: Argo wins Best Picture Oscar
trajectory.description: Directed and starred in 'Argo,' which won the Academy Award for Best Picture and earned him the BAFTA and Golden Globe for Best Director.

trajectory.title: Batman in DCEU
trajectory.description: Began portraying Batman in 'Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice' and subsequent DCEU films through 2023.

trajectory.title: Air and continued directing
trajectory.description: Directed and starred in 'Air' (2023) about Nike's signing of Michael Jordan, continuing his acclaimed filmmaking career.

name: Elio de Angelis
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Italian Formula Three Championship in 1977 at age 19, made his Formula One debut with Shadow at the 1979 Argentine Grand Prix at age 20, and won his first F1 Grand Prix (1982 Austrian GP) at age 24, establishing himself as a top-tier racing driver by his mid-twenties.
starting_point: Born in 1958 in Rome, Italy; came from a wealthy family; son of a prominent Italian architect; pursued racing despite family expectations.
current_position: Died on May 15, 1986 at age 28 in a testing accident at the Paul Ricard circuit in France; final status: F1 driver for Shadow, Lotus, and Brabham with 2 Grand Prix victories.

trajectory.title: Italian Formula Three champion
trajectory.description: Won the Italian Formula Three Championship, establishing himself as a top junior racing talent in Italy.

trajectory.title: F1 debut with Shadow
trajectory.description: Made his Formula One debut with Shadow at the 1979 Argentine Grand Prix, quickly impressing with his pace.

trajectory.title: Joined Lotus
trajectory.description: Signed with Lotus, one of F1's most prestigious teams, partnering with Mario Andretti and later Nigel Mansell.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory at Austrian GP
trajectory.description: Won his first Grand Prix at the 1982 Austrian Grand Prix at the Österreichring, holding off Keke Rosberg.

trajectory.title: Third in World Championship
trajectory.description: Finished third in the 1985 F1 World Championship with Lotus, his best championship result, scoring two podiums.

trajectory.title: Moved to Brabham and fatal accident
trajectory.description: Joined Brabham for 1986 but was killed in a testing accident at Paul Ricard on May 15, 1986, when his car's rear wing failed at high speed.

name: Mariah Carey
milestone_by_age_26: Released her debut album 'Mariah Carey' in June 1990 at age 21, which reached #1 on the Billboard 200 and produced four #1 singles; won Grammy Awards for Best New Artist and Best Female Pop Vocal Performance in 1991.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Huntington, New York; mother was a vocal coach and opera singer of Irish descent; father was an aeronautical engineer of African-American and Venezuelan heritage; parents divorced when she was 3.
current_position: American singer, songwriter, and producer; one of the best-selling music artists of all time with over 200 million records sold; known as the 'Songbird Supreme'; continues performing and recording.

trajectory.title: Signed with Columbia Records
trajectory.description: Demo tape passed to Columbia Records executive Tommy Mottola, who signed her and began developing her career.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Mariah Carey'
trajectory.description: Released debut album which reached #1 on the Billboard 200 and produced four #1 singles: 'Vision of Love,' 'Love Takes Time,' 'Someday,' and 'I Don't Wanna Cry.'

trajectory.title: Grammy Awards for Best New Artist
trajectory.description: Won Grammy Awards for Best New Artist and Best Female Pop Vocal Performance, establishing her as a major star.

trajectory.title: Music Box and 'Hero'
trajectory.description: Released 'Music Box,' which became her best-selling album with over 28 million copies worldwide, featuring the hit 'Hero.'

trajectory.title: Daydream and 'Fantasy'
trajectory.description: Released 'Daydream,' which featured 'Fantasy' (her first #1 debut on the Hot 100) and 'One Sweet Day' with Boyz II Men, which spent 16 weeks at #1.

trajectory.title: Butterfly and artistic control
trajectory.description: Released 'Butterfly,' marking her transition to more R&B and hip-hop influenced sound and greater creative control.

trajectory.title: The Emancipation of Mimi comeback
trajectory.description: Released 'The Emancipation of Mimi,' a massive commercial comeback that won three Grammy Awards and sold over 12 million copies.

trajectory.title: 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' #1
trajectory.description: 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' (1994) finally reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming a recurring annual chart-topper and cultural phenomenon.

name: George Michael
milestone_by_age_26: Wham!'s debut album 'Fantastic' reached #1 on the UK Albums Chart in July 1983 when Michael was 20, following hit singles 'Young Guns (Go for It)' and 'Wham Rap!'
starting_point: Born in 1963 in East Finchley, London; son of a Greek Cypriot restaurateur; met Andrew Ridgeley at school and formed Wham! in 1981.
current_position: Died on December 25, 2016 at age 53 from heart failure; final status: one of the best-selling music artists of all time with over 115 million records sold.

trajectory.title: Formed Wham! with Andrew Ridgeley
trajectory.description: Formed the pop duo Wham! with school friend Andrew Ridgeley, beginning their musical partnership.

trajectory.title: Wham! debut album 'Fantastic' #1
trajectory.description: Wham!'s debut album 'Fantastic' reached #1 on the UK Albums Chart, following hit singles 'Young Guns' and 'Wham Rap!'

trajectory.title: 'Careless Whisper' and 'Last Christmas'
trajectory.description: Released solo single 'Careless Whisper,' which topped charts in 25 countries, and Wham!'s 'Last Christmas,' which became an enduring holiday classic.

trajectory.title: Wham! concert in China
trajectory.description: Wham! became the first Western pop act to perform in China, a historic cultural milestone.

trajectory.title: Solo debut album 'Faith'
trajectory.description: Released debut solo album 'Faith,' which sold over 25 million copies and won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

trajectory.title: Listen Without Prejudice
trajectory.description: Released 'Listen Without Prejudice Vol. 1,' a more introspective album that showcased his artistic range and led to a legal battle with Sony.

trajectory.title: Public coming out and 'Outside'
trajectory.description: Came out publicly after an arrest in Beverly Hills and released the single 'Outside,' addressing the incident with humor.

trajectory.title: Retirement from public performance
trajectory.description: Largely withdrew from public life and active music promotion, though continued recording sporadically.

trajectory.title: Death
trajectory.description: Died on December 25, 2016 at his home in Goring-on-Thames from heart failure, mourned worldwide as one of pop music's greatest voices.

name: Phil Collins
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Genesis as drummer in August 1970 at age 19, recording multiple albums including 'Nursery Cryme' (1971), 'Foxtrot' (1972), and 'Selling England by the Pound' (1973), and became lead vocalist in 1975 at age 24.
starting_point: Born in 1951 in Chiswick, London; received a toy drum kit at age 5 and a proper drum kit at 12; trained as a child actor at the Barbara Speake Stage School, appearing in 'A Hard Day's Night' (1964) as an extra.
current_position: English retired musician; drummer and lead vocalist of Genesis; successful solo artist with over 100 million records sold; retired from touring due to health issues.

trajectory.title: Joined Genesis as drummer
trajectory.description: Joined Genesis as drummer in August 1970, answering an ad in Melody Maker, and recorded on their albums throughout the early 1970s.

trajectory.title: Became Genesis lead vocalist
trajectory.description: Took over as lead vocalist after Peter Gabriel left Genesis, initially on a temporary basis before becoming the permanent frontman.

trajectory.title: Solo debut 'Face Value'
trajectory.description: Released debut solo album 'Face Value,' featuring the hit 'In the Air Tonight,' which became a defining track of the 1980s.

trajectory.title: Live Aid dual performance
trajectory.description: Performed at both Wembley Stadium (with Sting) and Philadelphia (solo) on the same day at Live Aid, flying across the Atlantic by Concorde.

trajectory.title: No Jacket Required and global stardom
trajectory.description: Released 'No Jacket Required,' which won three Grammy Awards including Album of the Year and sold over 25 million copies.

trajectory.title: Left Genesis
trajectory.description: Departed Genesis to focus on his solo career, though he would reunite with the band in 2007 for the 'Turn It On Again' tour.

trajectory.title: Retirement from music
trajectory.description: Announced retirement from music due to health issues including nerve damage in his hands and hearing problems.

trajectory.title: Genesis reunion and final tour
trajectory.description: Reunited with Genesis for 'The Last Domino?' tour in 2021-2022, the band's final performances, performing seated due to health issues.

name: Sebastian Vettel
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2008 Italian Grand Prix at age 21, becoming the youngest-ever F1 race winner at the time, and became the youngest-ever Formula One World Champion in 2010 at age 23. By age 26 he had won three consecutive World Championships.
starting_point: Born in 1987 in Heppenheim, Germany; began karting at age 7; received sponsorship from Red Bull's junior driver program, which funded his progression through junior formulae.
current_position: German former racing driver; four-time F1 World Champion (2010-2013); retired from F1 in 2022; active in environmental and social causes.

trajectory.title: Junior European Karting Championship
trajectory.description: Won the junior European Karting Championship, catching the attention of Red Bull's talent spotters who enrolled him in their junior driver program.

trajectory.title: Formula BMW ADAC champion
trajectory.description: Dominated the German Formula BMW championship with 18 wins from 20 races, an unprecedented level of dominance.

trajectory.title: F1 debut with BMW Sauber
trajectory.description: Made his F1 debut at the US Grand Prix, scoring a point on debut as a stand-in for the injured Robert Kubica, before moving to Toro Rosso.

trajectory.title: Youngest-ever F1 race winner
trajectory.description: Won the 2008 Italian Grand Prix at Monza with Toro Rosso from pole position, becoming the youngest-ever F1 race winner at age 21.

trajectory.title: Youngest-ever World Champion
trajectory.description: Became the youngest-ever Formula One World Champion by winning the title-deciding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, clinching the 2010 championship with Red Bull.

trajectory.title: Second World Championship
trajectory.description: Dominated the 2011 season to become the youngest double world champion, winning 11 Grands Prix.

trajectory.title: Fourth consecutive World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his fourth consecutive title with 13 Grand Prix victories including a record nine consecutive wins, becoming the youngest four-time champion in F1 history.

trajectory.title: Joined Ferrari
trajectory.description: Signed for Ferrari, replacing Fernando Alonso, and won three races in his first season with the Scuderia.

trajectory.title: Retirement from Formula One
trajectory.description: Retired from F1 after 16 seasons with 53 Grand Prix victories, 57 pole positions, and four World Championships, announcing his retirement before the final races.

name: Sade
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Diamond Life' on July 16, 1984 at age 25, which became one of the best-selling debut albums of the 1980s, selling over 10 million copies worldwide and winning the 1985 Brit Award for Best British Album.
starting_point: Born in 1959 in Ibadan, Nigeria; father was a Nigerian economics university lecturer, mother an English nurse; moved to England at age 4 after parents separated; studied fashion design at Saint Martin's School of Art in London.
current_position: Nigerian-British singer-songwriter; CBE; lead vocalist of the band Sade; one of the most successful British female artists in history; continues to release music intermittently.

trajectory.title: Joined band Pride
trajectory.description: After completing fashion design studies, began singing backup with the British band Pride, developing her performing style.

trajectory.title: Formed the band Sade
trajectory.description: Split from Pride with Stuart Matthewman, Paul Denman, and Paul Cook to form the band Sade, debuting at Ronnie Scott's Club in London.

trajectory.title: Signed with Epic Records
trajectory.description: Secured a recording contract with Epic Records after attracting record company attention with performances of 'Smooth Operator.'

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Diamond Life'
trajectory.description: Released 'Diamond Life' on July 16, 1984, which sold over 10 million copies worldwide and won the 1985 Brit Award for Best British Album.

trajectory.title: Second album 'Promise' and first Grammy
trajectory.description: Released 'Promise,' which hit #1 in both the UK and US, and won the band's first Grammy Award.

trajectory.title: 'Love Deluxe' and 'No Ordinary Love'
trajectory.description: Released 'Love Deluxe,' featuring the hit 'No Ordinary Love,' which won a Grammy Award and became one of their signature songs.

trajectory.title: 'Lovers Rock' and Grammy win
trajectory.description: Released 'Lovers Rock' after an eight-year hiatus, winning the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album.

trajectory.title: 'Soldier of Love' comeback
trajectory.description: Released 'Soldier of Love' after a ten-year gap, debuting at #1 in the US and winning the Grammy for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group.

trajectory.title: Commander of the Order of the British Empire
trajectory.description: Was made CBE in the 2017 Birthday Honours for services to music, having sold over 75 million records worldwide.

name: Mikhail Khodorkovsky
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Bank Menatep in 1989 at age 26, one of the first privately owned commercial banks in Russia, after establishing a successful import-export business and the Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development in 1987 at age 24.
starting_point: Born in 1963 in Moscow; son of two engineers; studied at the Mendeleyev Chemistry Institute; began his career in the Komsomol (Communist Party youth organization) apparatus during the Soviet era.
current_position: Exiled Russian businessman, oligarch, and opposition activist; resides in London; founded Open Russia to promote civil society; was Russia's richest man before his imprisonment.

trajectory.title: Founded Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development
trajectory.description: Established an import-export business under the Komsomol umbrella, exploiting the economic liberalization of perestroika to build early wealth.

trajectory.title: Founded Bank Menatep
trajectory.description: Founded one of Russia's first privately owned commercial banks, which became the foundation of his business empire.

trajectory.title: Acquired Yukos oil company
trajectory.description: Gained control of Yukos, Russia's second-largest oil company, through the controversial 'Loans for Shares' privatization scheme for approximately $350 million.

trajectory.title: Founded Open Russia
trajectory.description: Established the Open Russia Foundation to build and strengthen civil society in Russia, signaling his shift toward political activism.

trajectory.title: Arrested and charged with fraud
trajectory.description: Arrested at gunpoint by Russian authorities on charges of tax evasion and fraud after publicly challenging Putin on corruption; was at the time Russia's richest man with $15 billion.

trajectory.title: Sentenced to nine years in prison
trajectory.description: Found guilty of fraud and tax evasion and sentenced to nine years in prison; Yukos was broken up and its assets sold to state-owned companies.

trajectory.title: Second conviction and extended sentence
trajectory.description: Convicted of embezzlement and money laundering, extending his prison sentence to 2014; Amnesty International declared him a prisoner of conscience.

trajectory.title: Pardoned and exiled
trajectory.description: Pardoned by Putin after lobbying by former German foreign minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher, flown to Germany, and went into exile in London.

trajectory.title: Hague arbitration ruling
trajectory.description: The Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled that Russia had violated international law by taking Yukos from its shareholders for political purposes.

name: Neymar
milestone_by_age_26: Made professional debut at 17 in March 2009, won the Copa do Brasil at 18 (2010) as top scorer, won the Copa Libertadores at 19 (2011) as Best Player, and was voted South American Footballer of the Year in 2011 and 2012, all well before 26.
starting_point: Born in 1992 in Mogi das Cruzes, São Paulo, Brazil; son of a former professional footballer; joined Santos youth academy at age 11; was offered a move to Real Madrid at 14 but Santos convinced him to stay.
current_position: Brazilian footballer; Brazil's all-time leading goalscorer (surpassing Pelé); currently plays for Santos FC; previously played for Barcelona, PSG, and Al-Hilal; widely regarded as one of the greatest players of his generation.

trajectory.title: Joined Santos youth academy
trajectory.description: Joined the Santos FC youth system, where he developed into one of Brazil's most highly regarded young talents.

trajectory.title: Professional debut for Santos
trajectory.description: Made his professional debut for Santos in March 2009, scoring his first goal in his third game.

trajectory.title: Copa do Brasil winner and top scorer
